title: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling

sections.skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling

questions.skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A school wants to model the total cost of a field trip by bus. Name the quantities the model needs, with a unit for each.
questions.prompt_markup:
A school wants to model the total cost of a field trip by bus.
Name the quantities the model needs, with a unit for each.
questions.correct_answer: The number of students (students), the students each bus holds (students per bus), the cost of each bus (dollars per bus), and the admission price (dollars per student).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form: any complete, sensible set of quantities, each with a unit.

questions.skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A club rents a room for $300 and pays $40 for each member who attends. Its cost model is C = 40n + 300. Define C and n, with units.
questions.prompt_markup:
A club rents a room for $300 and pays $40 for each member who attends. Its cost model is C = 40n + 300.
Define C and n, with units.
questions.correct_answer: C is the total cost in dollars; n is the number of members who attend.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording, with both units.

questions.skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Which quantity best describes how fast a phone battery runs down?
questions.prompt_markup: Which quantity best describes how fast a phone battery runs down?

choices.text: Number of apps on the phone
Percent of charge used per hour
Width of the screen in inches
Mass of the phone in grams

questions.correct_answer: Percent of charge used per hour
questions.grading_note: A rate of drain needs an amount of charge per unit of time.

questions.skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Two towns have different populations and different areas. Define one quantity, with units, that compares how crowded they are.
questions.prompt_markup:
Two towns have different populations and different areas.
Define one quantity, with units, that compares how crowded they are.
questions.correct_answer: Population density: people per square mile (or per square kilometer).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent quantity that is people per unit of area.

questions.prompt: Kilowatt-hours per month is a sensible quantity for a model of a household's electricity use.

sections.skill: Write and solve px + q = r from a word problem

questions.skill: Write and solve px + q = r from a word problem
questions.prompt: A gym charges a $25 fee plus $10 per class. Tom paid $95. How many classes did he take?
questions.prompt_markup:
A gym charges a $25 fee plus $10 per class. Tom paid $95.
How many classes did he take?
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. 25 + 10c = 95 gives c = 7.

questions.skill: Write and solve px + q = r from a word problem
questions.prompt: A phone costs $50 plus $15 per month. The total so far is $140. For how many months has it been paid?
questions.prompt_markup:
A phone costs $50 plus $15 per month. The total so far is $140.
For how many months has it been paid?
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. 50 + 15m = 140 gives m = 6.

questions.skill: Write and solve px + q = r from a word problem
questions.prompt: A plumber charges a $12 fee plus r dollars per hour. A 3-hour job costs $57. Which equation fits?
questions.prompt_markup:
A plumber charges a $12 fee plus r dollars per hour. A 3-hour job costs $57.
Which equation fits?
questions.grading_note: 3 hours at r dollars is 3r, plus the $12 fee.

questions.skill: Write and solve px + q = r from a word problem
questions.prompt: x = 6 is the solution of 4x + 6 = 30.
questions.prompt_markup: x = 6 is the solution of 4x + 6 = 30.

questions.skill: Write and solve px + q = r from a word problem
questions.prompt: x = 3 is the solution of 2x - 5 = 11.
questions.prompt_markup: x = 3 is the solution of 2x - 5 = 11.
questions.grading_note: 2 · 3 - 5 = 1; the solution is x = 8.

questions.prompt: A rectangular garden needs an area of at least 200 square feet and can use at most 60 feet of fence. Does a 10 ft by 20 ft garden meet both requirements? Explain.
